doc.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Playing swing dances with Sun Ra at the Baby Grand
summary: Harrison played Ellington and older tunes with Sun Ra at the Baby Grand Ballroom in Harlem and was called for social dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: That’s right. That’s right. I would talk about it. “This guy’s crazy, this guy’s nuts.” But guess what? He turned me on — I played a gig with him at a place called the Baby Grand in Harlem and we had to play a dance, we had to play like Duke Ellington and Fletcher Henderson, we had to play swing and a little bebop. Because he’d play like, he could play like Art Tatum on piano you know. Fletcher — you know he could play stride. Kind of remind you of Monk in a way, Thelonious Monk in a way, where he could play the stride. And that was really where — he was that age, he came out of the swing era. I mean he was born at that particular period in time so he could play like a Duke Ellington or a Fats Waller or you know that real swing. So he knew I could play these tunes, so we went and

played, it was called the Baby Grand Ballroom on 125th Street in Harlem, and we were playing “Satin Doll” and “It Don’t Mean a Thing” and some of those older tunes. And he liked the way I played that, when he played changes now. So I got to play tunes and he really liked that. You know I made the gig, really made it happen for him. He was very pleased. So a lot of times he’d call me to play these traditional dances, for social dancing. The people, you know two step foxtrots and all that kind of stuff. Tangos and all that kind of stuff.
